source_text.body:
Support academic social science work with a coding agent setup
A social scientist shares a Claude Code configuration they built to support much of their academic work, such as analysis and writing.
·
Nov 25, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
BK Lee's repo installs a Claude Code and Cursor configuration for R, Stata and Python work. It includes a global CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, commands and a hook. The workflow is plan-based: the agent asks questions, the researcher and coauthors revise a written plan, the agent runs it in a sandbox, and the researcher checks results against the plan. Other agents (/codex, /gemini) review the plan.
How it went
The source reports no measured results. It gives the setup and counts: 12 core skills, 10 optional ones, 14 plugins and 14 Cursor extensions. It warns that agent code can still be wrong and that citations need manual checking.
Worth knowing
Claude Code bills through Anthropic API credits, not a Pro subscription. Default sandbox mode suits sensitive data; full-autonomy mode skips the sandbox.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Help me set up this folder as a research workspace for my [field, e.g. political science] work. Create a CLAUDE.md that records my conventions: [analysis tools, e.g. R or Python], citation style [style], writing voice [description], and folder layout for data, code, and drafts. Add a few reusable commands for jobs like [e.g. cleaning survey data, running a regression table, editing a paper section]. Finish by walking me through the setup and a test run on [a sample file], and ask before overwriting or deleting any existing file.
Original source: https://github.com/letitbk/claude-academic-setup
